Author, what grade are you currently in at school? Most successful SCP writers have familiarity with college-level writing skills, since clinical tone (a basic requirement for a standard format SCP article) is typically covered in college.

If you haven’t encountered clinical tone or writing analytical essays in school yet, it can be hard to write an article that possesses the "flash fiction as written by a professional scientist" tone the site audience is looking for. item.title: Re: Robot Refugees From Outer Space
item.content:encoded:
Hello Dootboy96! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: Three extraterrestrial lifeforms mechanical in nature claiming to be millions of years old and a machine they refer to as "The Forge" have been recently detained. Apparently they are the last remaining members of their species, and the Forge is their last hope of saving it. The Forge is a highly advanced piece of technology that is the robots' main method of reproduction, able to practically 3D print new members of their species under the correct circumstances. According to the three, Earth has the perfect conditions to incubate the Forge. However, the Forge supplies itself with the materials necessary to undergo such processes by absorbing and thaumaturgically converting large amounts of matter. Due to the catastrophic implications of letting a machine like this function on Earth, consuming the world's resources, the Foundation has concluded that the Forge must be destroyed ASAP before a GH-O 'Dead Greenhouse' Scenario could occur. There is only one problem, though: the Forge is nigh-indestructible by conventional means. But the Foundation is quickly looking into ways of solving this problem.

My main issue here is the Foundations motive to have the machine destroyed, while using it does pose a threat to life on earth, there isn't really any clear indications that the skips were going to use it no-matter what (in fact they sounds very civil). Considering there isn't a clear danger to keeping it around, it sounds more plausible that it would just be kept in containment. -The Foundation would only really destroy something if they absolutely had too, considering the skips sound reasonable/negotiable its odd they would be so set on destroying it.

Along with this, I feel the skips themselves aren't really expanded on or explained much. Currently, they're only really shown fighting off the Foundation? which (to me) makes the narrative feel a bit flat, along with making the 'aliens' themselves feel a bit cliched.- Currently nothing really separates them from the "they're going to invade us" trope.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The three aliens learn they must race against the clock to breach containment, secure the Forge, and escape the Foundation before the machine is destroyed, sealing their species' fate for good. However, if they successfully incubate the Forge on Earth, it could very well mean the end of organic life as we know it.

As for the narrative, there isn't really enough of an arc here to get an idea of happens or how this would look in a draft. There doesn't seem to be much on where and how the skips were found, what actually takes place (there isn't really a clear progression here?), and what everything is building up to.

In general, I would recommend developing the skips a little more. perhaps show a bit more their journey across space, why and how they found earth and what the consequence of them not operating here would be. Allow the audience to get a feel for what and who they are, rather than just painting them as what essentially boils down to "aliens that are trying to invade earth".

- perhaps this could work a bit better if the conflict was more focused on the Foundations containment than anything? maybe they only want to leave in search of an easier place to populate, but the Foundation refuses, or is very reluctant to let them leave?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.content:encoded:
An idea for an ever-changing bottle of cleaning supplies that could be deadly if used incorrectly…

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

It is a safe-class object.
It manifests as a random bottle of cleaning supplies consistent with several non-anomolous brands of cleaning supplies.
It causes horrible injuries to people who use the bottle's contents for any purpose other than cleaning.
Injuries range from lacerations to third-degree burns on your face.
Can change form when unobserved for a period of ██ to █ hours

Safe
Central Narrative:
In a foundation sweep of a anomalous materials distribution operation in █████, ██████. The object was found in a janitorial closet in the building where the operations were taking place. The object in question was at the time taking the form of a bottle of clorox-brand bleach. On the return to site-██ It had changed into the form of a bottle of windex. It's dangerous properties were discovered when during a test of it's chemical composition the researcher spontaneously combusted and suffered lacerations. Further tests concluded that the object was only dangerous when being used in a way the object's label did not support.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
An everyday object that will never hurt you if you use it right, But if you dare step out of line, A painful punishment awaits.

item.title: Re: Sword Ballerina (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Hello Impperatrix! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block


The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A woman-like automaton that also can transform into a sword and fights using ballet moves. It always has a host/owner. The host experiences memories and has skills of the anterior hosts. The SCP's main action is protecting its current host.

Overall, theres quite a few elements here, and not all of them really feel linked with each other? I'm unsure on why it can transform into a sword, why it fights specifically with ballet moves, why it needs a host and why its main motive is to protect the owner.

As it stands these aspects feel sort of meaningless, as the skip doesn't really seem to have a purpose for most of them, nor does it really have a reason for protecting its hosts.-why is it so set on that?

That said, I quite like the idea that the skip passes down memories from previous owners. However, this aspect isn't really explored or focused on much in the narrative (at least not from what I can see). Which as a result makes the effect (and the skip to an extent) feel a bit flat.- does the skip pass down memories from other hosts kept in containment?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The narrative is more centred on the hosts, the "SCP-XXXX-A". There will be three hosts. As the story progresses, the Foundation tries to contain the SCP as experiments with its owners. The owners start presenting some dangerous behaviors, the Foundation has to protect them more and more from themselves and from the SCP influence. Every owner iteration changes the article, including some description and containing methods.

Overall, there isn't really an arc here? while I like the approach taken conflict wise, there isn't really much explaining or expanding on where and how the skip was found, what is actually tested or why and how the characters keep getting experimented on (considering the narrative seems to imply the skip escapes multiple times?) and how the narrative ends.-whats the payoff here? how will the ending make me as the reader feel?

Along with this, I'm finding it a bit hard to get invested in the characters, as they don't really get established much. What will makes me as the reader care about them? what makes them interesting? how do they initially become a host?- what ends up happening to them?

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most of the time, the hosts actions are more connected to the Foundation's experiments and protocols than the SCP itself:

The first host uses a deprivation tank to revive ancient owners' memories, thus developing PTSD.
The second host used to test the SCP's protection abilities, becoming paranoical and/or even homicidal.
The last owner is treated as an object, being constantly protected and losing his free will.

This makes the Foundation look kind of cruel. As they don't seem to have much of a reason to be treating the skip and its hosts so harshly, what are they gaining from this? why is it more important to them than the skips wellbeing?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

I’d say the agent would be questioning the way The Foundation contains humanoid anomalies and the way it treats d-class.

My tentative recommendation would be to throw together a specific incident of some kind. That way, the holder's "confession" can be more emotional than a monologue about ethics and practices. Bonus points if you can tie it into the theme of subjective good and evil.

Personal destinies are things that people are always meant to do. They may not know on the beforehand, but they always feel very satisfied when they’re done.

If we disregard terminology, is this still destiny at all? Was the 'holder' destined to overthrow the site administrator? Were those small GOIs fated to crumble due to a single silly locket? Or is it just what happens as a consequence of an anomaly? In other words, how large-scale do the effects of personal destinies get before they stop being personal?

item.title: Re: What is Love?
item.content:encoded:
You mostly got it right, the celebration of Valentine's Day as a whole essentially is the ritual. The more people that celebrate it, the less damage the fallen god does. Here's a rough outline of how I picture the story progressing, I just found out "What Is Love" was already taken by 031 so I'll come up with a different title later.

Object Class: Euclid, as the containment procedures relatively don't require much work on the Foundation's part.

Special Containment Procedures: It's stated here that the Valentia Protocol must be enacted on an annual basis at all costs, and low-level memetic agents are to be disseminated within advertising in all known forms of media with ethics committee approval of regime change operations in [REDACTED (several Middle Eastern countries that banned V-day)] in conjunction with the United States government currently pending.

+ show block
– hide block

Description: The section begins with a seemingly unrelated Foundation investigation in 1965 into the ritualistic suicides of Bronze Age archaeologists following expeditions into Jordan leading to the discovery of SCP-5XXX-1, the ruins of a civilization that displeased the entity in the past and consequently collapsed in on itself as a result with the lingering effects inflicting severe anxiety, low self-esteem, and suicidal tendencies on anyone within proximity too low on the Psionic Resistance Index to resist it. Further attempts to gain insight into its nature eventually resulted in the capture of SH saboteurs attempting to stop them from disturbing its “resting place” and the Foundation being alerted to the existence of SCP-5XXX.

Interview Log 1: Discussion between a captured SH operative and a Foundation researcher regarding the GOC termination attempt in early 1953 spearheaded by occultists who would later go on to form The United Church of Satan, Scientist. The next two decades were marked by escalating conflicts between SH cells that worshipped the deity seeking revenge and the GOC. SCP's supposed neutralization called into question.

Description continued: Reiteration of the elevator pitch

Interview Log 2: Communication between the Foundation and GOC attempting to confirm the neutralization of the entity, statistics utilized by the Foundation to disprove their claims, distrust on both sides leads to little progress.

Incident Log 1: Several members from the subsections of the three organizations involved in the investigation are found to have killed themselves and/or others.

Interview Log 3: Three-way communication between the organizations, with the Foundation essentially acting as a mediator several times throughout. Valentia Protocol established.

Experiment Log 1: Valentia enacted in Sweden, 1966. Marriage rates continue to decline, divorce rates continue to climb, failure.

Experiment Log 2: Valentia enacted in Japan, 1970. Initial results show promise.

Experiment Log 3: India, 1992. Massive success.

Experiment Log 4: Pakistan, 1996. Moderate success, government interference complicating data collection.

Experiment Log 4: Iran, 2009. [REDACTED]

Incident Log 2: A valentine's card is left on the project head's desk on Valentine's Day 2014, reading "If you all ever really loved me you'd let me die." Global decline continues.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: What is Love?

Thanks! After starting with a Euclid, which happened because the idea I came up with ended up being that, I intentionally wrote Safe, Keter, and Thaumiel next as I proceeded through all the recognized classes. I then went off the deep end with all the esoterics I could bundle together in my normal-length arms with relatively small hands, which is turning out to be nearly all of them. I think the classes work really well as creative prompts. If you were to come up with a Safe, what would it be? What would be so dangerous as to necessitate a Keter class? This isn't to say you should start with the class and then write the SCP — in most cases that's an abominable idea — but as an experiment, I've found it pretty inspirational. My highest-rated SCP exists because I forced myself to think: what's a Tiamat?

I had fun with the log format; SCP-5751 is a spiritual sequel in that regard. The idea of telling these mini-stories, and making them little puzzles for the reader to unravel, excited me. I've taken it up a notch in the companion tale series to this skip, starting with Character Development. Turns out the answer to the question I asked myself at the start of writing this article — "How many weird ideas can you think of based on an unforgettable password?" — is "a lot."

item.title: New Writer, New SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Hi, my name is Teddy and I've had this idea for an SCP for awhile now, and I really want to get people's input on it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre(s): Horror, Drama, etc

Page Layout: I plan on using the standard sort of SCP formatting that I've seen for most other articles use.

Elevator Pitch: My main idea is I want to create an SCP that plays on my somewhat odd fear of being kidnapped and subsequently brainwashed/conditioned to be someone else's family member, primarily their child. The SCP in question appears to most individuals as their most beloved parental figure in life (parent, older sibling, etc), but to people who have never had any sort of positive role model, the SCP appears in her true form, which resembles a humanoid insect. Upon the SCP meeting such a person, she will pull them into a hug, and after five minutes of being embraced, the victim is physically and mentally regressed to the state of an infant, whom the SCP will then raise as it's own until the victim reaches adulthood.

The SCP in question actually isn't secretly eating the kids or something like that, but she’s still scary in that what she’s doing is meant to be beneficial to the victim, at least from her perspective. I'm not sure if I'm expressing this very well here, but what makes her scary is how nice she is, in that she could give you a better childhood, but at the cost of who you’ve become.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Like I've kinda already hinted at, the theme here is one of brainwashing, and how the SCP clearly believes she’s doing the right thing by reraising the individuals she chooses to “adopt”, but she does so (almost always) without consent.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I feel like while kidnapping and child abuse are major themes in a lot of horror stories, nothing I've seen quite captures the fear of seemingly being “rescued” by your abductor. It wasn't the victim's decision to start over, but now that they have, is it moral to just give in and accept your new life, or to fight back? Are you somehow now responsible for your abduction if you accept it? Are you selfish for fighting back when you've been shown almost nothing but love and affection? These are the sorts of questions I want to present to the reader.

Additional Notes: I worry I'll make the SCP too Mary Sue-like, so I would appreciate some advice here!

All criticism is welcome here, and I'd love to get some advice from those of you with more experience. Again, I'm a newbie here, but I've been doing creative writing since about 2013, so I like to think I'm not going into this completely blind.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeking Greenlight - Mayan Blues
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Historical-Fiction, Exploratory

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout w/ exploration/interview logs (tentative format)

Elevator Pitch:
SCP is a pigment of "Mayan Blue" color developed and mass produced in the early 1900s by a now defunct chemical company. A chemical mystery for many years, the company appears to have uncovered a long lost technique dating back to the Mayan's that creates the pigment, which carries unexpected anomalous properties. These properties carry over to any object painted or colored with the pigment. Any surfaces colored with the blue will act as a sort of dimensional rift, with objects able to pass through into it. While most objects do not have enough painted surface area to pose major physical risk, if an individual were to pass through completely, they would find themselves in another dimension. In particular, a dimension that seems to largely be the inspiration for much of Mesoamerican mythology; populated with many entities from those myths.The land has also been settled long ago by none other than the Mayans themselves, a people who history recounts as seemingly having disappeared near the decline of their civilization.

Show More
Show Less

Central Narrative:
For years, the foundation has contained a number of the pigmented objects and has largely erased the existence of the pigment from record. Over time, the anomalous affects have faded from all objects large enough to pass through and connection with the other world has been lost; all attempts to recreate the pigment have proved futile. That is until in the late 1900's a university researcher and avid collector of "rare colors" stumbles across an un-found document on the pigment and attempts to recreate it thinking the pigment had simply been lost to the ages. The researcher eventually succeeds and unwittingly stumbles into the other world after painting his office wall. The incident ends up on the desk of the Foundation and an expedition into the rift is launched with the hopes of retrieving the professor so that they may acquire his knowledge on the creation of the pigment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The search-and-rescue exploration into an alternate dimension housing the not only living myths but a long thought "deceased" civilization.

Additional Notes: While I have done quite some research for the concept, I am by no means an expert on the history of pigments nor on Mesoamerican history/culture. If anyone happens to be more well versed on either subject, your feedback is very much welcome.

item.title: Sword Ballerina (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama, Narrative-driven.

Page Layout (Optional): As other narrative-driven SCPs, the page will have different iterations of the SCP article.

Elevator Pitch: A woman-like automaton that also can transform into a sword and fights using ballet moves. It always has a host/owner. The host experiences memories and has skills of the anterior hosts. The SCP's main action is protecting its current host.

Central Narrative: The narrative is more centred on the hosts, the "SCP-XXXX-A". There will be three hosts. As the story progresses, the Foundation tries to contain the SCP as experiments with its owners. The owners start presenting some dangerous behaviors, the Foundation has to protect them more and more from themselves and from the SCP influence. Every owner iteration changes the article, including some description and containing methods.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most of the time, the hosts actions are more connected to the Foundation's experiments and protocols than the SCP itself:

  • The first host uses a deprivation tank to revive ancient owners' memories, thus developing PTSD.
  • The second host used to test the SCP's protection abilities, becoming paranoical and/or even homicidal.
  • The last owner is treated as an object, being constantly protected and losing his free will.

Additional Notes: I want to know if you think the SCP is weak for being focused on its "owners". Also, I want to know if the narratives are interesting or if in its anachronic file-based narrative the story will become boring.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: The Indiscernible Infection
item.content:encoded:
The Indiscernible Infection

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type SCP article

The infection is untraceable and can not be detected in the tissues of infected members. The infection spreads by another human being in close contact with an infected individual the exact radius is unknown. Once an individual is within close contact with an infected they will begin to stare blankly in the distance for roughly thirty seconds. After this, they will begin their previous actions. Infected individuals speak in an unknown language, possess no knowledge of past loved ones or acquaintances, and ignore noninfected individuals. People suffering from amnesia are immune to the infection's effects.

Will Include: Virus origins, containment procedures, and experiment log.

Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Elevator Pitch:A humanoid with a human body, except the skin area covering the collarbone and above has been replaced with teil scales. item.title: Re: A small question
item.content:encoded:
Does anyone know why this is said,

Because readers don't find the material interesting? If something doesn't interest them on the mainsite, they're not obligated to explain exactly why the piece didn't spark their interest. If someone is expecting thorough critique from a reviewer, the forums and IRC chatrooms are the place to look.

because I am curious as to whether this helpful to the author

While it's not the most helpful feedback, it's more helpful than nothing at all. Disliking something for not being interesting enough is different from disliking something for being too long-winded and a slog to read, or disliking something because it uses a color scheme or unique format that is disorienting or difficult to follow.

as one person could find it disinterestong but the next could find it absolutely fascinating.

Just because some people find something interesting does not mean everyone else has to feel the same way, and vice versa. People can disagree with others about the kind of article they like to read. Sometimes an author has to just shrug and accept a downvote. Just because someone else likes something does not make it wrong to dislike the same thing for personal preference reasons.

item.title: Re: Deer in the mist (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Just a heads up, we already have SCP-3502 (The Kangaroo Sign) which plays on the same premise of "animals that are often hit by people in vehicles get their revenge on said vehicles and people" but does not rely on the shock horror of deaths.

What you have here feels like a fairly common urban legend, which might be workable based on the imagery of the deer (though we already have some well-known anomalous deer on the mainsite (you can see them in this listing: http://www.scpwiki.com/system:page-tags/tag/cervine) but is also kind of bland given that it relies on typical horror genre tropes like the mysterious mist, accidentally harming allies/family while trying to harm something else(the movie Oculus ends with this), and the overly convenient found journal.

Personally I recommend delving more into the lore of the deer from a different perspective, maybe a colony of wildlife creatures who consider it their guardian, or the like. A Group of Interest article might be a better format for something like this.
